text:
Anna Li: saw a weird skew in yesterday's AB run — assigned 10/90 but observed ~6/94 for the canary.
Devin Clarke: ugh, notation: assigned vs observed can be different if routing header dropped. any logs?
Anna Li: pulling traces now, but CanaryBot already flagged a drift: `alert: sample_ratio_deviation 0.04` (pinned).
CanaryBot: METRIC SNAPSHOT: canary:10% assigned, observed:6.2%, control:93.8% — 12k requests sampled, stratified by region.
Maria Gomez: interesting that it's asymmetric. quota or retry routing could bias towards control. did we change ingress proxy last deploy?
Victor Park: we rolled a small proxy patch two days ago to default preserve X-Routing but only for /v2 endpoints. AB uses /internal/exp which might not have header passthrough.
Sam Patel: that matches — internal/exp flows through the old path that strips `x-rollout-id`. If header missing, router falls back to hash-based key on user_id which is very uneven for our test users.
Mike Chen: can you dump a few request examples from the proxy logs? curious whether client side included rollout cookie or header.
Anna Li: pasted a filtered log snippet: ```
2026-03-17T23:12:02Z proxy-01 DROP_HEADER x-rollout-id user=12345 path=/internal/exp
2026-03-17T23:12:02Z proxy-02 PASS_HEADER x-rollout-id user=67890 path=/v2/generate
```
Devin Clarke: yep — some proxies updated, others haven't. that explains region stratification too (eu region still on old proxy).
Maria Gomez: so root cause = uneven proxy rollout -> sample ratio mismatch. What's the decision: abort canary, or continue but account for imbalance in analysis?
Sam Patel: can't trust metrics if assignment not stable. my vote: pause traffic split and re-route all AB traffic to stable router until we fix passthrough.
Victor Park: creating a short patch to ensure `x-rollout-id` preserved for /internal/* paths. I'll push canary to proxy fleet now.
DeployBot: deploy started for proxy-preserve-rollout (canary) — id=deploy-20260317-7721 :rocket:
Anna Li: while that's rolling, we should decide on end criteria changes for the experiment. Observed counts will change once proxies are consistent.
Mike Chen: proposal: require both (1) sample ratio within 1.5% absolute of assigned for 30m rolling window AND (2) min N per variant = 2k, before final analysis.
Devin Clarke: add an instrumentation check: if any intermediate routing hop reports dropped rollout headers > 0.5% over window, mark instrumentation drift and auto-hold.
Maria Gomez: for stat test itself — current p-value based threshold has been confusing for PMs. suggest an A/B stop rule: minimum runtime 4 hours OR min N and then use Bayesian credible interval for metric delta with 95% prob of improvement or harm.
Sam Patel: pragmatic: we can keep p-value for alerts but require human ack + instrumentation check before auto-rollout.
Anna Li: agreed. immediate actions: 1) Victor to finish proxy canary (in progress), 2) DeployBot to run a sampling integrity check after proxy roll, 3) pause automated rollouts if sample_ratio_deviation > 0.02.
Victor Park: proxy canary finishing — 3 of 4 datacenters updated. will verify header preservation now.
CanaryBot: RESCAN COMPLETE: observed after patch: assigned 10.0%, observed 9.7% (n=4,200). sample_ratio_deviation=0.003.
Anna Li: great — small deviation now. I'll re-run the analysis with the corrected counts.
Mike Chen: for the run analysis, let's re-weight using assigned-probabilities only if sample ratio deviation < 0.01; otherwise treat as instrumentation failure.
Devin Clarke: note for tooling: add a telemetry card in Console per rollout showing 'routing header integrity' and a small heatmap of proxies that dropped headers.
Maria Gomez: I'll file a tiny Product ticket for the Console UX tweak and the new stop rules. cc @Sam @Anna for details.
Sam Patel: thanks — once Console shows integrity we can automate the final pass. :thumbsup:
Anna Li: final note: we should also add an experiment pre-check that simulates assignment for a small synthetic load and validates observed==assigned within tolerance before exposing to real traffic.
Victor Park: noted. adding to infra backlog.
Anna Li: ok closing this thread for now — will post final analysis when re-run completes. :eyes:
